policy_name: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
question: To what extent will the 'safety frameworks' published by these organizations be scrutinized by independent bodies or governments to validate their adherence to the stated commitments, and what will be the criteria for assessing their adequacy?

The safety frameworks published by these organizations will be subject to scrutiny by independent bodies and governments to validate their adherence to the stated commitments. The criteria for assessing their adequacy will include:

1. Compliance with the commitments outlined in paragraphs I-VI, as detailed in the Frontier AI Safety Commitments (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, paragraph VIII).
2. Alignment with relevant international agreements to which the home governments of the organizations are party (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, paragraph II).
3. The adequacy of risk assessments, thresholds definition, and mitigation effectiveness (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, Outcome 1, paragraphs I-IV).
4. The adequacy of internal accountability and governance frameworks, and the resources assigned to ensure adherence to the commitments (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, Outcome 2, paragraph VI).
5. The transparency of the implementation of the commitments, except in cases where doing so would increase risk or divulge sensitive commercial information to a degree disproportionate to the societal benefit (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, Outcome 3, paragraph VII).
6. The involvement of external actors, such as governments, civil society, academics, and the public, in the process of assessing the risks of their AI models and systems, the adequacy of their safety framework, and their adherence to that framework (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, Outcome 3, paragraph VIII).

The specific process and frequency of these assessments are not detailed in the Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, but it is stated that organizations will provide transparency on this, including their reasons, through public updates (Source: Frontier AI Safety Commitments document, paragraph VII).

2. Increasing significantly the number of students, including graduate level and Ph.D. candidates, in data assimilation (Section 305(d)(2)(B)).
3. Utilizing modern software and frameworks for data assimilation research and development (Section 305(d)(2)(C)).

6. Establishing mechanisms to enable all members of the consortium to archive and access data required to support the work under this subsection (Section 305(d)(2)(F)).

These actions will foster a growing data assimilation workforce, address critical research challenges, and facilitate collaboration between NOAA and the research community, ultimately leading to advancements in data assimilation research and operations.

policy_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence")
question: How will the identified capability and skill gaps (as per Section 1554(b)(5)) be addressed to ensure the successful development and adoption of AI applications for cyber missions?
answer_low_temp:
The identified capability and skill gaps will be addressed by the following means:

1. Identification of the gaps: The roadmap and implementation plan will identify the current capability and skill gaps that must be addressed prior to the development and adoption of AI applications for cyber missions (Section 1554(b)(5)).

2. Inclusion in research and development processes: Opportunities will be identified to solicit operator utility feedback through inclusion into research and development processes, and wargaming or experimentation events (Section 1554(b)(6)).

3. Formalized process for capturing and tracking lessons learned: A formalized process will be established for capturing and tracking lessons learned from such events to inform the development community (Section 1554(b)(6)).

4. Maturity model: A maturity model describing desired cyber capabilities, agnostic of the enabling technology solutions, will be defined, including phases in the maturity model or identified milestones (Section 1554(b)(8)).

5. Collaboration with relevant developers: Areas for collaboration with relevant commercial off the shelf and government off the shelf developers will be identified to address requirements supporting capability gaps (Section 1554(b)(8)).

6. Synchronization and coordination: The roadmap and implementation plan will be synchronized and coordinated to be consistent with section 1509, which may provide additional guidance on addressing capability and skill gaps (Section 1554(c)).

7. Classified briefing: The Commander and the Chief Information Officer will provide a classified briefing to the congressional defense committees on the roadmap and implementation plan, which may include details on how the identified capability and skill gaps will be addressed (Section 1554(d)).

Sources:
- Title XV, Subtitle A, Section 1554, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (NDAA 2021)
- https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/house-bill/6395/text
answer_high_temp: The identified capability and skill gaps will be addressed by outlining them in the roadmap and implementation plan (Section 1554(b)(5)). The plan will include a formalized process for capturing and tracking lessons learned from research and development processes, wargaming or experimentation events (Section 1554(b)(6)). Additionally, the plan will identify opportunities for soliciting operator utility feedback to inform the development community (Section 1554(b)(6)).

policy_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 909 ("Ensure IC Directives Account for AI and ML Tools in Intelligence Products")
question: What criteria will the Director of National Intelligence use to determine if existing Intelligence Community Directives adequately guide analysts on the use, sourcing, and transparency of AI/ML tools in intelligence products?
answer_low_temp:
The Director of National Intelligence will use the following criteria to determine if existing Intelligence Community Directives adequately guide analysts on the use, sourcing, and transparency of AI/ML tools in intelligence products:

1. Sufficient guidance and direction on how to properly use AI/ML tools: The Director will assess whether the existing directives provide clear instructions on the appropriate application of AI/ML tools in the production of intelligence products.

2. Provision of sourcing information about AI/ML tools: The Director will evaluate whether the directives require analysts to disclose the use of AI/ML tools in their intelligence products, including information about the specific tools used, their capabilities, and any limitations.

3. Transparency to customers regarding the use of AI/ML tools: The Director will determine whether the directives ensure that the users of intelligence products are informed about the role of AI/ML tools in the creation of those products, including any potential biases, errors, or limitations.

Citation: The criteria are derived from the text of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (H.R. 6395), specifically Section 909 (a)(1)(A) and (B).

Additionally, the Director will determine if any of these directives require an update to provide such guidance and direction.
